GEOLOGY
Paleomagnetic Study of Devonian and Carboniferous Rocks
of the Southern Urals: An Independent Test of Collision between
the Magnitogorsk Island Arc and the Passive Margin
of the Continent of Laurussia
I. V. Golovanovaa,*, K. N. Danukalova, Corresponding Member of the RAS V. N. Puchkova,
A. M. Kosareva, and R. Yu. Salmanovaa
Received December 20, 2017
Abstract—New paleomagnetic data on Devonian and Lower Carboniferous rocks of the Magnitogorsk Zone
(Southern Urals) are presented. The paleomagnetic pole calculated for the Lower–Middle Devonian is quite
close to the coeval pole of the Baltica Paleocontinent (Laurussia), which indicates that the Magnitogorsk
island arc was probably located close to the continent, but not being accreted with it. Paleomagnetic data
obtained for Lower Carboniferous rocks may indicate that the Magnitogorsk island arc was turned in the
Early Carboniferous and collided with the continent of Laurussia forming a single continent.
DOI: 10.1134/S1028334X18090052

Fig. 1. Simplified structural–tectonic map of the Southern Urals showing sampling sites. Inset: the position of the Baltica paleo-
continent with the Precambrian basement (shown in gray), the Urals, and the study area (SU). 1, Boundary between the first-
order structures; 2, boundary between the second-order structures; 3, major tectonic faults. The Main Ural Fault is shown by a
thick dashed line. Sampled sections: 4, Devonian; 5, Carboniferous; 6, sampling site Kaga; the paleomagnetic directions for this
site were recalculated using the data from [7]. Abbreviations in the map: UF—Uralian Foredeep; WUFTZ—West Uralian Fold
and Thrust Zone; BMA—Bashkir Meganticlinorium; ZS—Zilair Synclinorium; UA—Uraltau anticlinorium; MMS—Magni-
togorsk Megasynclinorium; M1—Voznesenka–Sakmara Zone; M2, M3—West Magnitogorsk Zone: М2—Irendyk subzone;
М3—Kizil–Urtazym subzone; M4—Central Magnitogorsk Zone; M5—East Magnitogorsk Zone; EUZ—East Uralian Zone.
